s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of generalized painful skin lesions with systemic symptoms and liver dysfunction
salient_findings: Generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions
Yellow scleral discoloration
Fever following removal of a tibial implant
Development of pruritus and fluid-filled rashes after starting ciprofloxacin
Icterus with elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels
key_facts: 22-year-old man
15-day history of generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions
7 days of yellow scleral discoloration
1 month of fever following removal of a tibial implant
History of tibial fracture treated with internal fixation
Surgical-site infection and persistent fever after implant removal
Initial treatment with paracetamol without relief
Development of generalized pruritus and fluid-filled rashes after starting ciprofloxacin
Denial of angioedema, dyspnea, abdominal distention, lower-limb swelling, hematemesis, melena, altered sensorium, alcohol use, or immunocompromise
Afebrile with stable vital signs on examination
Icterus without pallor, clubbing, cyanosis, lymphadenopathy, or dehydration
Multiple generalized vesicles and bullae with non-hemorrhagic crusts over the trunk and extremities
Leukocyte count 18,520/mm3 with neutrophils 64%, lymphocytes 22%, and eosinophils 12%
Hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, platelets 423,000/mm3
Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels

differentials: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis due to ciprofloxacin
per_call: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis due to ciprofloxacin

shortlist.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient developed generalized pruritus and fluid-filled rashes after starting ciprofloxacin, and the extent of skin and mucosal involvement meets criteria for TEN

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: The patient has a similar presentation to TEN, but with less severe skin and mucosal involvement

shortlist.label: DRESS syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: The patient has a history of drug exposure and developed a rash, fever, and systemic symptoms, which are consistent with DRESS syndrome

shortlist.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient developed a generalized rash with pustules after starting ciprofloxacin, which is consistent with AGEP

shortlist.label: Severe cutaneous adverse reaction
shortlist.why_kept: The patient has a severe skin reaction with systemic symptoms, which is consistent with a severe cutaneous adverse reaction

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions, yellow scleral discoloration, and mucosal involvement, along with the timeline of developing these symptoms after ciprofloxacin exposure, are consistent with toxic epidermal necrolysis. The extent of skin and mucosal involvement, as well as the laboratory findings, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
rejected.why: While similar to TEN, SJS typically involves less body surface area and the patient's presentation suggests a more severe reaction

rejected.label: DRESS syndrome
rejected.why: DRESS syndrome usually presents with a longer latency period after drug exposure and often includes lymphadenopathy and eosinophilia, which are not prominent in this case

rejected.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
rejected.why: AGEP is characterized by numerous small, sterile pustules and typically lacks the severe mucosal involvement and widespread epidermal necrosis seen in this patient

rejected.label: Severe cutaneous adverse reaction
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes TEN, SJS, and other severe reactions, but the specific details of the patient's presentation point more directly to TEN
